output.name: Ketha
output.myth: Kael the Netter cast for fallen stars every night off the Leeward Reach, and every night they slipped his mesh like wet fish. He went to Ennu the Kite-Wright and asked for a better needle. Ennu gave him a mending shuttle of bone, pointed at both ends, with thread wound round its belly. "Work with it," said Ennu, "and your hands will never be idle." Kael mended cords all night with Halvet, the Lantern Boat, low to the south, where three women and a boy once went for nets. He never caught a star. But at dawn the shuttle was gone from his fingers, and a thread ran from its place straight up toward the Unflown Kite, whose cloth Ennu cut for Aun. Hesk, who keeps count at the pole, has marked it. Some say the shuttle still mends up there, and the thread is a line let out for the drowned to climb. Fishers who lose a man tell the Netter his name and wait. He gives no one back. But he listens, which is more than the sea does.
output.finding: Find Halvet, the Lantern Boat, low in the south of the Leeward Reach, then go a fist and a little more north of it to reach Ketha, the Mending Shuttle.
